2B.10 We are to put our trust in God as our help and shield (for he who trusts in the LORD, mercy shall surround him).
2D.10 It is vanity and foolish to make and worship idols or graven images.

precepts.text: I am the Lord, that is My name, and My glory will I not give to another; the graven images are the idols.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory”. The Most High says the same of himself: “I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.”

The graven images are the idols of the psalm, silver and gold, the work of men's hands. His glory goes to his name alone, not to another, and his praise is not for graven images.

precepts.text: To whom will you liken God? The workman melts a graven image, but it is the Most High that sits upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants are as grasshoppers; He brings the princes to nothing.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.” Isaiah asks, “To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him? The workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold, and casteth silver chains. He that is so impoverished that he hath no oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a cunning workman to prepare a graven image, that shall not be moved.”

That is the idol: a workman melts it, a goldsmith spreads gold over it, a poor man picks a tree that will not rot. Then the contrast: “Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning?” “It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in: That bringeth the princes to nothing; he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.”

Our God is in the heavens and has done whatsoever he has pleased. It is the Most High that sits upon the circle of the earth, with the inhabitants as grasshoppers, and he brings the princes to nothing. The idols have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not.

precepts.text: Because of these idols the Most High said He would scatter us among all people and there we would serve other gods of wood and stone.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

Because of these idols, the Most High said he would scatter us among all people and there we would serve other gods of wood and stone. That is the idolatry the psalm describes, spoken of throughout the scriptures, and it followed us into the scattering: idols with mouths that speak not and eyes that see not, and they that make them are like unto them.

precepts.text: The graven image is a teacher of lies, so the entertainers, athletes, and dope boys flossing with the jesus piece around their neck are carrying a teacher of lies.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?”

The graven image is a teacher of lies. So the entertainers, athletes and dope boys flossing with the jesus piece around their neck are carrying a teacher of lies, a dumb idol with a mouth that speaks not. “They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.”

precepts.text: This is one of those lies learned under the false image, telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” This is one of those lies learned under the false image, the teacher of lies: telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.

That is what the graven image teaches. The psalm says our God is in the heavens and his glory is not unto us but unto his name, for his mercy and for his truth's sake, and they that trust in the image are like unto it.

precepts.text: When we are in the land of our enemies the Most High will not cast us away nor destroy us utterly, but will remember the covenant of our ancestors.
precepts.point: This is so important because we are not a cursed people; we are a people under the curses. Because the Lord has been mindful of us, let us see how He has been mindful.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath been mindful of us: he will bless us; he will bless the house of Israel”. This is so important, because we are not a cursed people; we are a people under the curses. Here is how he has been mindful of us.

“And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God.” Even in the land of our enemies, under the curses, the Most High will not cast us away nor destroy us utterly. He remembers the covenant of our ancestors. That is why Israel and the house of Aaron and all that fear the Lord can trust in him: he is their help and their shield.

precepts.text: This is one of the promises that belong to us as Israelites, the covenants and the promises.
precepts.point: This is so important because we are not a cursed people; we are a people under the curses. Because the Lord has been mindful of us, let us see how He has been mindful.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”. The covenants and the promises belong to us as Israelites.

That the Lord has been mindful of us and will bless the house of Israel is one of those promises. He will not cast us away in the land of our enemies, because the covenant is ours.

precepts.text: The Most High told Balaam not to curse the people for they are blessed, refusing to let the king of Moab hire a curse upon Israel coming up out of Egypt.
precepts.point: The heavens are the Lord's, but the earth He has given to the children of men. The dead praise not the Lord, but we will bless the Lord from this time forth and forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“He will bless them that fear the Lord, both small and great. The Lord shall increase you more and more, you and your children.” The scriptures say we are blessed, not cursed. “And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed.”

The king of Moab tried to hire a curse upon Israel coming up out of Egypt, and the Most High refused to let it happen: they are blessed. This speaks of us as a nation, not of the brother or sister in the midst of sin claiming to be blessed and highly favored.

precepts.text: Our seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and all that see them shall acknowledge that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed.
precepts.point: The heavens are the Lord's, but the earth He has given to the children of men. The dead praise not the Lord, but we will bless the Lord from this time forth and forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.”

The Lord increases us more and more, us and our children, and our seed shall be known among the Gentiles. All that see them shall acknowledge that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed. We are blessed of the Lord which made heaven and earth, and we will bless the Lord from this time forth and for evermore.

points: Not unto us but unto His name give glory, for His mercy and His truth's sake. The heathen ask where is now their God, but our God is in the heavens and He has done whatsoever He has pleased.
